stem:
The diagram shows Falguni's square sheet of side $12\,\mathrm{cm}$ with centre marked $O$. She wants a circular arc of radius $3\,\mathrm{cm}$ with centre $O$, drawn with a compass.

Which claim correctly states where the compass point must be placed and what radius is needed?

options.text: Place the compass point at $O$ and open the compass to radius $3\,\mathrm{cm}$.
Place the compass point at a corner of the square and open it to $12\,\mathrm{cm}$.
Opening the compass to $3\,\mathrm{cm}$ is what creates the centre $O$.
Freehand sketch quality settles the arc, so the compass point may be anywhere.

teacher.key_rationale: An arc with centre O and radius 3 cm needs the compass point at O opened to 3 cm. A corner with opening 12 cm omits the intended centre and radius. Saying the opening creates O reverses the relation. Freehand quality is outside this hinge.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source triangle into a labelled square with centre O and dashed arc of radius 3 cm.
